The cleanest minimal fix that matches the existing code style: wrap the single target_info into a hash. But we need to be careful about the key. Looking at `existence_path`:

```ruby
def existence_path
  hash = {}
  @tails.each_key {|target_info|
    if @follow_inodes
      hash[target_info.ino] = target_info
    else
      hash[target_info.path] = target_info
    end
  }
  hash
end
```

So the hash key is `target_info.ino` (if follow_inodes) or `target_info.path`. 

But wait, at line 422, the `target_info` is the original one passed in (with the inode from `expand_paths`). The `tw` was set up with this `target_info`. But `@tails[target_info] = tw` was NOT executed (because the ENOENT happened before). So `@tails.delete(target_info)` would return nil.

However, the purpose of calling `stop_watchers` here is to detach and close the watcher `tw` that was just created by `setup_watcher`. But `stop_watchers` looks up `tw` from `@tails`, which doesn't have it! So even if we fix the `each_value` error, the watcher `tw` won't be detached/closed because `@tails.delete(target_info)` returns nil.
